knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Dust settles on both faces of a slat. A face that is missed shows as a line in light.
Lowering the blind and angling the slats gives access to both faces for the two passes.
A slight-angle check shows residual lines that a straight-on look may miss.

practicalCriteria: Lowers the blind fully, angles the slats downward, and dusts both faces in the two planned passes.
Uses a short-handled duster and handles the cords and bottom rail gently.
Checks the blind from a slight angle and re-dusts any visible line.
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80% pass mark, which for three questions means all three correct. Practical sign-off is separate and observed by an assessor.
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation of one blind dusted in full
Blind dusting entry on the route sheet
stopWorkCriteria: Worker climbs onto a window sill to reach a blind
Blind left with visible dust lines after the check
